layers.name: Infrastructure & Configuration
layers.description: This layer encompasses files related to environment setup, Docker orchestration, dependency management, and general application configuration. It defines how the application is built, deployed, and configured.

layers.name: Data Access & Models
layers.description: This layer is responsible for defining the application's data structures (ORM models) and managing database connections and sessions. It acts as the interface between the application's business logic and the persistent storage.

layers.name: Core Services & AI Engine
layers.description: This layer contains the primary business logic, including AI model abstractions, the chat engine, document creation utilities, the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline, and knowledge base management. It forms the intelligent core of the application.

layers.name: API & User Interface
layers.description: This layer handles external interactions, including defining API endpoints (webhooks, admin routes) and rendering the user-facing web interface. It manages request routing, data presentation, and user interaction.

layers.name: External Integrations
layers.description: This layer focuses on specific integrations with external platforms, such as the Zalo messaging API. It provides the necessary functions and bot logic to communicate with and respond to external services.

layers.name: Batch Jobs & Utilities
layers.description: This layer contains standalone scripts and utilities for various operational tasks, including database migrations, data seeding, knowledge base re-indexing and ingestion, document generation, and automated testing.

layers.name: Documentation & Static Assets
layers.description: This layer includes all non-code files that provide information about the project, user guides, architectural overviews, and static resources like document templates or data files used by the application.

tour.title: Project Setup and Initial Configuration
tour.description: Begin by understanding how the project is set up and configured. This includes environment variables, Docker orchestration for deployment, and the main entry point of the FastAPI application. This step covers how the application is built and launched.

tour.title: Data Model and Persistence Layer
tour.description: Next, explore the application's data structures and how information is stored and managed. This involves examining the SQLAlchemy ORM models, the database connection utilities, and the initial SQL schema for setting up the database.

tour.title: External Integrations: The Zalo Bot
tour.description: Understand how the application interacts with external messaging platforms, specifically Zalo. This step focuses on the webhook endpoints that receive messages and files, and the Zalo API service responsible for sending responses.

tour.title: Core AI: RAG Pipeline and AI Engine
tour.description: Dive into the intelligence of the system. This step covers the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline, including embedding generation, semantic search, and question classification. It also introduces the AI engine that abstracts interactions with various LLMs.

tour.title: Chat and Knowledge Management
tour.description: Learn how user chat sessions are managed, from creating new sessions to retrieving chat history. This step also explores the knowledge manager, which handles document parsing, ingestion into the knowledge base, and overall document lifecycle.

tour.title: Document Creation and Generation
tour.description: Examine the functionality for generating new documents. This includes services for analyzing images, normalizing names, and programmatically creating Word documents based on templates and extracted metadata.

tour.title: Administrative Interface and Monitoring
tour.description: Understand how administrators interact with and monitor the system. This covers the admin API routes, the web templates for the dashboard, document management, chat sessions, and the audit logging mechanism for tracking system actions.

tour.title: Batch Jobs and Utility Scripts
tour.description: Finally, review the collection of standalone scripts used for various operational tasks. These include database schema migrations, re-indexing embeddings, ingesting documents, seeding initial data, and automated testing.
